name: a.l.l.ure head spa & studios
address_raw: 8981 Daniels Center Dr, Suite 204, Fort Myers, FL 33912
address_source: Confirmed independently via Apple Maps place page (place-id I84F676C08286B829), matching the address given in the task brief and the business's own Square Online site metadata.
email_note: Could NOT independently confirm this address in any raw HTML I fetched directly this session: it does not appear in the Square Online site's HTML/bootstrap state, nor in the giftly.com listing page HTML (both checked directly with curl/WebFetch). It surfaced consistently (with matching phone and address) across two separate WebSearch queries, which suggests a search-engine-indexed source (likely Yelp or a directory page) that direct fetch could not reach: Yelp returned HTTP 403 on every attempt (curl and WebFetch, matching the task brief's note), and mbasic.facebook.com/Facebook returned a login wall or error on every attempt. Given the phone and address attached to the email were correct in both independent search results, confidence is moderate but not fully verified against a raw source page. Used as the outreach contact per instructions, with this caveat disclosed.
website_check: Re-verified this session: curl -D on https://allureheadspa.com/ shows a 301 redirect to http://allure-head-spa.square.site/ which itself 302-redirects to https://allure-head-spa.square.site/ (a Square Online site-builder page, generator meta tag confirms 'Square Online'). No independent custom domain serves original content; the vanity domain is purely a redirect shell into the Square subdomain. Per pipeline rule, square.site subdomains do not count as an owned website. Confirmed has_own_site: false.
hours: Monday-Friday 9:00 AM-5:00 PM, Saturday 9:00 AM-5:00 PM, Sunday Closed
hours_source: Taken from the business's own Square Online site content (siteData.page cell 'location-hours' block, fetched and parsed directly from the site's server-rendered bootstrap state this session). Apple Maps independently lists a slightly different Saturday hour (10:00 AM-5:00 PM) with the same Sunday-closed and Mon-Fri 9-5 pattern; the business's own published hours were used as primary since they are the more authoritative first-party source, with the minor Saturday discrepancy noted.
about: a.l.l.ure head spa & studios is described across multiple sources as Fort Myers, Florida's first multi-room head spa, open since 2024, with several private studios so guests can book solo, as a couple, or bring a friend for a 'Bestie Sesh' head spa session. The business offers head spa (scalp) treatments, facials and skin care (including a professional Dermalogica line and microneedling packages), and lash services, all via online booking on Square.
about_source: Cross-referenced across multiple WebSearch summaries (consistent 'first multi-room head spa', 'Bestie Sesh', 'established 2024' language appearing verbatim across several independent search results) and the business's own Square Online site content (membership/service descriptions fetched directly).

services_source: The Square Online storefront (allure-head-spa.square.site) is a fully client-rendered SPA: category pages (Head Spa Services, Skin Care Services, Lash Services, Add-Ons, Memberships) and product detail pages return an empty template shell with no products/prices in server-rendered HTML (confirmed by fetching and parsing window.__BOOTSTRAP_STATE__ on every category and product URL in the site's own sitemap.xml; commerceLinks.products was empty on all of them). What IS server-rendered is each product's <title> and meta description, which was used verbatim for the descriptions above. This is a real, structural limitation of the platform, not a research shortcut: no exact price list is publicly fetchable for the core head spa/skin/lash line items. The one concrete price found ($60) is explicitly an upgrade fee within the Monthly Bliss membership, not a standalone treatment price, and is presented as such (not as a menu price). 'Bestie Sesh' as a real named group-treatment service was corroborated across at least 3 independent WebSearch result summaries but its own product/description page could not be located in the sitemap.
cta_note: Primary booking CTA points to https://allure-head-spa.square.site/ (their real Square Online storefront/booking page) throughout the site, per has_own_site: false and no separate booking-platform link found.
reviews_note: No verbatim, named reviews were found after an extensive search: Yelp (yelp.com/biz/allure-head-spa-and-studios-fort-myers) returned HTTP 403 on every attempt (curl with Chrome UA, WebFetch, mobile m.yelp.com variant); Facebook page and post permalinks are login-walled for WebFetch/curl except one specific indexed post permalink (facebook.com/61563950637271/posts/122118826340465021/) which showed engagement counts (3 reactions, 3 shares) but no visible comment text or reviewer names. Google Maps/Search knowledge panels could not be scraped directly (blocked/JS-rendered). giftly.com's own review widget for this listing shows '0.0 stars (0)' reviews. One indexed WebSearch snapshot of the Facebook page showed 'Not yet rated (1 Review)' at some point, consistent with this being a very new business with limited review volume on any single platform. Per pipeline rule ('si hay menos de 3 [reviews], mostrar las que haya'), since zero verbatim quotes could be sourced, none are fabricated or displayed as testimonials; the reviews/testimonials section of the site was adapted to feature verified real facts about the business instead of quotes, and links out to Google Maps for visitors to read reviews directly.
language_source: All sourced text (Square site descriptions, search result summaries, Apple Maps listing, giftly.com listing) is in English. Fort Myers, FL is an English-language market with no Spanish-language signal found in any source.
review_count_note: This figure was provided in the task brief as sourced from a third-party aggregator (localheadspa.com) and could NOT be independently corroborated this session despite trying a second source as instructed: Yelp blocked (403) on every attempt; Google Search/Maps knowledge panels are not scrapable via WebFetch/curl (blocked or JS-only); localheadspa.com's own site was checked directly and does not actually contain a listing for this business (searched site:localheadspa.com, only unrelated FL salons found); giftly.com's own review count for this listing shows 0; one indexed Facebook snapshot showed 'Not yet rated (1 Review)' at some point. Given the business is confirmed to have opened in 2024 and has very limited public review presence on every platform actually reached this session, the 4.7/85 figure should be treated as low-to-moderate confidence, single-source, and NOT independently confirmed on live Google Maps. It is presented on-site with an explicit caveat ('reported across spa directories, not yet independently confirmed on Google') rather than asserted as a confirmed Google rating.

images.source: Instagram was blocked on every attempt (web_profile_info API returned a rate-limit message, WebFetch on the profile page returned HTTP 429, and both IG mirrors imginn.com/picuki.com returned HTTP 403), exceeding the pipeline's 2-attempt limit before moving on. Yelp and the main Facebook page/photos tab are login-walled or blocked (403/login wall) for both curl and WebFetch. Real photos were ultimately recovered from two sources: (1) the business's own Square Online site content, which server-renders its 'about' section image directly in window.__BOOTSTRAP_STATE__ (a real photo of a client mid scalp-facial treatment, originally published by the business with a promotional text overlay and logo watermark that were cropped out to isolate the clean underlying photograph); (2) one specific Facebook post permalink that WebSearch surfaced and that loaded directly via WebFetch/curl (unlike the main FB page), containing a real photo collage of two genuine treatment moments (a client relaxing under a purple LED head-spa dome, and a close-up scalp massage with shampoo) which were cropped out of their polaroid-style graphic frame. The business's own logo and icon mark (teal 'a.' symbol) were pulled directly from the Square site's bootstrap state as native, uncompressed brand assets.

discarded: The Square site's own hero banner image (a generic stock-styled flat-lay of towels, candles and oils): excluded as it reads as licensed stock photography rather than a real photo of this specific business, and the site's own JSON referenced an Unsplash attribution block nearby suggesting a stock source.

The uncropped 'Scalp facial.png' image: excluded in its original form because roughly half the frame is covered by the business's own bold promotional text ('BOOK YOUR SCALP FACIAL SESSION') and a logo watermark, which the pipeline's gallery curation rule prohibits (no text/caption overlays in gallery tiles). Used only after cropping to isolate the clean photograph underneath.

3 additional crop attempts from the same source photo (fixture close-up, mid-frame, base-of-basin close-up) were discarded for either still showing text overlay or being too abstract/low-content to read well as a standalone tile.
Instagram feed photos: never retrieved, all 3 access paths blocked this session (see images.source note).
images.curation_note: Only 6 real, verified image assets could be recovered for this very new (2024-opened), digitally minimal business after exhausting Instagram, Yelp, Facebook page/photos and giftly.com as sources: 2 native brand marks (logo, icon) and 4 crops from just 2 underlying real photographs (1 Facebook collage with 2 inset photos, 1 Square-site photo). This falls short of the 6-14 target photo COUNT nominally, though the raw distinct source photography is genuinely limited to 2 photos for a brand-new business with almost no public photo footprint. All 4 photo crops were visually inspected one by one: no selfies, no clutter, no screenshots with text/caption overlays in the final selections (all text and watermarks were cropped out), and the one 'eyes closed' shot used (about-facial.jpg) is a calm, well-lit, editorial-style relaxation pose rather than an unflattering mid-procedure shot. The gallery section was deliberately reduced to a single featured wide tile rather than padded with repeated or low-quality images, per the pipeline's explicit guidance to prefer fewer sections with good photos over filling with bad ones.

brand_vibe: The business's own logo and icon are teal (#679399-ish) and sage green (#81B767-ish) on transparent background, in a soft serif/script style, conveying a calm, botanical, zen spa identity. The real photos recovered show warm, moody interior lighting (deep mauve/wine curtain backdrop, a striking purple LED head-spa dome, copper fixtures) rather than a bright, white-walled spa look. Combining the brand's teal identity with a dark, moody base (rather than a bright white one) suits both the logo and the real photographed ambiance: a dark charcoal-teal background with a teal/sage accent, mirroring the design system's dark-v2 approach (similar structure to gold-on-dark or blue-on-dark builds, here teal-on-dark).

palette.name: allureheadspa
palette.notes: Teal/sage accent derived directly from the business's own logo colors (sampled: teal #679399, green #81B767), on a dark charcoal-teal base. Merktop footer badge kept gold/untouched per design system rule.

build_base_template: templates/dark-v2/index.html (Pure Artistry skeleton): chosen over templates/light-v2/index.html because the real recovered photography shows a moody, dark-lit interior (purple LED dome, deep warm tones) that suits a dark base better than a bright clean one, and dark-v2 already ships the bilingual data-es/data-en mechanism with EN default, matching this English-language business, plus the full motion v2/v3 marker set (split-word, sec-num, tile-cap, cursor-ring, foot-mark, heroInner).
